name: Default string dtype (object -> str)
description: Columns of text are inferred as dtype str, not object. Code that tests dtype == object, is_object_dtype, select_dtypes(object), dtype.kind or isinstance on dtype takes another branch and can return different values.
minimal_example_idea: cols = [c for c in df.columns if df[c].dtype == object]; clean only those columns (str columns are skipped)
warn_evidence: 2.3.0 notes: future.infer_string=True is opt-in; no default warning stated (whatsnew v2.3.0 #avoid-numpy-object-dtype-for-strings-by-default)
pilot_tasks: drift in 18 tasks: t07 t08 t09 t10 t12 t15 t16 t26 t27 t30 t32 t33 t34 t35 t36 t40 t44 t48 (25 programs, qwen3.5-9b)
notes: Pilot label STR_DTYPE also contains astype(str) and isinstance(...,str) regexes, so S01 and S03 are merged in the pilot count; split by hand-check in the full study

name: Missing-value sentinel in str columns is always NaN
description: None in a text column becomes NaN under the str dtype (object dtype keeps None). Code that compares with None, uses "is None", or writes None back sees different values.
minimal_example_idea: df.city.map(lambda v: "none" if v is None else v) ; or (df.city == None) counts
pilot_tasks: t01 t05 t06 (missing city/status/category text)
notes: Notes say pd.isna and ordinary NA methods behave the same, so only exact-sentinel code drifts

name: astype(str) preserves missing values
description: astype("str") no longer turns NaN into the text "nan". Counts, value_counts, filters on "nan", concatenations and encodings on astype(str) output change.
minimal_example_idea: df.city.astype(str).str.title().value_counts()  (2.3: a "Nan" group; 3.0: NaN dropped) ; label-encode via astype(str)
warn_evidence: Listed as notable bug fix in migration guide; no 2.x warning stated
pilot_tasks: not separated per program in the pilot; invited by t01 t02 t09 t37 t38 t40 (text columns with missing values)
notes: Merged with S01 in pilot counts; full study should tag by hand-check or by a separate regex

name: Series.values returns an ExtensionArray for str
description: .values no longer a NumPy array for text columns; code using NumPy semantics (mask indexing, np.where on .values, ==) can behave differently or fail later.
notes: Effect size unknown; needs execution check (not run in this stage)

name: Regex methods on str dtype use ASCII-only \w \d \s \b in 3.0.x with pyarrow
description: With pyarrow-backed str dtype, regex classes matched only ASCII and $ handled trailing newline differently; fixed in 3.1.0 to match Python re (and pandas 2.x). So 3.0.x and 3.1.x differ on non-ASCII text.
minimal_example_idea: df.name.str.extract(r"(\w+)") on names with accents/Japanese characters; str.contains(r"^\w+$")
warn_evidence: 3.1.0 notable bug fix text; no 2.x warning stated
notes: Pilot fixtures: not checked for non-ASCII text; run the version split 3.0.x vs 3.1.x for this mechanism; needs a non-ASCII fixture

name: read_csv(dtype="category") infers numeric and boolean categories
description: Zero-padded ids or zip codes read as category lose leading zeros (now integer categories).
minimal_example_idea: pd.read_csv(f, dtype="category") on a column of codes like 00123; then categories.tolist()
notes: Only for 3.1 vs 2.3/3.0; rare in LLM code

name: Datetime resolution inferred: strings and stdlib datetime give datetime64[us]
description: Parsed dates are datetime64[us] instead of [ns]. Integer casts (astype("int64"), view("i8"), .value, .asi8) return values 1000x smaller; epoch seconds computed as //10**9 become 0 or wrong.
warn_evidence: no warning in 3.0 notes; 2.x notes: not found
pilot_tasks: drift: t21 t37 (qwen), t05 (Sonnet 5.5); invited by t17 t18 t19 t20 t37
notes: Pilot DT_UNIT label also covers D03 (t21 via Period.end_time)

name: Numeric input to to_datetime/to_timedelta/Timestamp: unit [s] in 3.0, [us] in 3.1
description: pd.to_datetime(ints, unit="s") gives datetime64[s] in 3.0 and datetime64[us] in 3.1 (ns in 2.x). Int casts and sub-unit arithmetic differ among 2.3, 3.0.x and 3.1.x.
warn_evidence: 3.1.0 text: change of the 3.0 behaviour; no 2.x warning stated
pilot_tasks: t18 asks for epoch output (not input); fixtures have no integer epoch column
notes: Pilot ran 3.0.6 and 3.1.1 but no task reads integer epochs. A fixture with epoch columns is needed

name: Period.to_timestamp / end_time resolution (us when possible)
description: Period.end_time and PeriodIndex.end_time change their actual value (nanosecond end vs microsecond end of period); month-end timestamps differ.
minimal_example_idea: df.d.dt.to_period("M").dt.end_time compared with a datetime or used as key
warn_evidence: 3.0 other API changes text; 2.x not found
pilot_tasks: t21 (qwen3.5-9b: to_period("M").dt.end_time)
notes: Attributed as DT_UNIT by the pilot

name: date_range / timedelta_range unit inferred, not ns
description: Unit comes from start, end and freq. Casts to int and comparisons with ns data differ.

name: Time zones are zoneinfo, not pytz
description: .tz returns zoneinfo.ZoneInfo; pytz-specific code (tz.localize, tz.zone) differs; ambiguous or nonexistent times raise ValueError.
notes: Fixtures are tz-naive; most failures would be loud (AttributeError), so silent share unknown

name: offsets.Day is a calendar day (DST aware)
description: Timestamp + Day(1) keeps wall-clock time across DST; date_range(freq="D") and resample("D") on tz-aware data around DST change; Day no longer equals Hour(24).
minimal_example_idea: pd.Timestamp("2025-03-08 08:00", tz="US/Eastern") + pd.offsets.Day(1)  (example in the notes)
notes: Needs tz-aware data spanning a DST change

name: to_datetime(strings, unit=...) parses like without unit
description: Strings with unit specified are no longer parsed into floats; parsed as dates.
warn_evidence: listed under 3.0 Removal of prior version deprecations (#other-removals); exact 2.x warning class not verified

name: select_dtypes("datetime64[ns]") selects only ns columns
description: In 3.1 the string spec "datetime64[ns]" names nanosecond resolution only; parsed dates are us, so such a call selects nothing (3.0 and 2.x selected all datetime columns).
notes: Interacts with D01; makes 3.1 differ from 3.0

name: infer_freq quarter-start anchor, isocalendar year dtype, UTC tzinfo repr, Timedelta.total_seconds ns
description: Small 3.1 changes: infer_freq reports QS-JAN instead of QS-OCT; isocalendar year int32; zero-offset strings give datetime.timezone.utc; Timedelta.total_seconds includes nanoseconds.
minimal_example_idea: pd.infer_freq(quarter_start_index) ; str of tz in output
notes: Low expected effect on LLM code

name: Series.dt.to_pydatetime returns a Series of datetime
description: Previously an ndarray of datetime objects; now a Series, so index alignment and later arithmetic differ.
minimal_example_idea: df.d.dt.to_pydatetime()[0] ; np.array ops on the result

name: Chained assignment df[col][mask] = v no longer updates df
description: The first indexing step is a copy, so the write is lost. Worked on pandas 2.x for column-then-mask order. SettingWithCopyWarning removed.
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.2.0 #chained-assignment: FutureWarning ChainedAssignmentError for df["foo"][mask] = v
pilot_tasks: invited by t41 t42 t43 t44 (UPD) and t05 t06 (IMP)
notes: Pilot label COW attributed 0 drift programs; the harness records pandas warnings, so this is the best-covered warned case

name: Chained inplace method df[col].fillna(x, inplace=True) no longer updates df
description: The intermediate column behaves as a copy, so inplace on it is lost. Very common in older LLM output.
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.2.0 #chained-assignment: FutureWarning for inplace method called in a chained manner
pilot_tasks: invited by t05 t06 t07 t43
notes: Regex for COW label includes inplace=True

name: Derived objects never share memory with the parent (view propagation)
description: Writes through a derived Series/DataFrame (column variable, slice, .values-based) no longer reach the parent, and vice versa.
minimal_example_idea: col = df["a"]; col.iloc[0] = 99; result = df  (2.x: df changed; 3.0: not)
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.3.0 #copy-on-write: warnings behind pd.options.mode.copy_on_write="warn" (since 2.2); not on by default
pilot_tasks: invited by UPD family, t43

name: Inplace methods return self instead of None
description: replace, fillna, ffill, bfill, interpolate, where, mask, clip with inplace=True return the object. A program storing the return value got None on 2.x.
minimal_example_idea: result = df.fillna(0, inplace=True)  (2.x: None; 3.0: the frame)
notes: On 2.3.3 result is None, so the program is excluded as no-result, not counted as drift

name: copy= keyword has no effect
description: copy=False in astype, reindex, rename, merge, etc. no longer shares data; deprecated.
minimal_example_idea: b = df.astype("float64", copy=False); b.iloc[0,0] = 0; compare df
notes: Only matters if the program mutates after copy=False

name: Index constructors copy ndarray inputs
description: Mutating the source array no longer changes the Index.
minimal_example_idea: arr = np.array([1,2]); idx = pd.Index(arr); arr[0] = 9; idx
notes: Rare in data-wrangling code

name: groupby observed default False -> True (categorical keys)
description: Groups for unused categories (from pd.cut, qcut, category dtype) vanish from results; counts and shares per bin change shape.
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.1.0 Other Deprecations: default of observed=False deprecated (FutureWarning when categorical keys)
pilot_tasks: t14 (1 program, qwen3.5-9b); invited by t13 t14 t15 t34 t33
notes: Full study needs sparse bins (empty categories) for the shape change to show

name: observed=False with several keys passes unobserved groups to apply/agg
description: NaN for unobserved key combinations becomes 0 (sum), 1 (prod), True (all), False (any).
minimal_example_idea: df.groupby(["key1","key2"], observed=False)[["values"]].apply(lambda x: x.sum()) with categorical key1
warn_evidence: 3.0 notable bug fixes text; no warning
notes: Needs categorical key and explicit observed=False

name: groupby.apply: grouping columns excluded (include_groups=False)
description: apply no longer passes the grouping columns to the function. Sums over all columns lose the key column; code reading g["key"] raises KeyError (loud).
minimal_example_idea: df.groupby("customer_id").apply(lambda g: g.sum(numeric_only=True))  (numeric key summed on 2.x, absent on 3.x)
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.2.0 Other Deprecations: including the groups in apply is deprecated (DeprecationWarning)
pilot_tasks: invited by t25 t26 t27 t28 t45 t47; KeyError loud breaks possibly from this (t07 t22 t27): not confirmed
notes: Pilot GROUPBY_APPLY label appears only in E2-E4 configs, not in the E1 primary result

name: as_index=False keeps groupings not in the input
description: Aggregations with as_index=False no longer drop groupings that are not columns of the frame (e.g. a Series or array key).
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.1.0 Other Deprecations (DataFrameGroupBy with as_index=False not including groupings)
pilot_tasks: t26 t29 t30 t45 (normalised key as Series)

name: agg/apply/transform no longer replace NumPy and builtin functions with pandas versions
description: groupby.agg(np.std) used pandas std (ddof=1); now NumPy std (ddof=0). np.std and np.var are the risky cases because the NumPy ddof default differs from pandas (stated by this catalogue as a hypothesis, to confirm by execution).
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.1.0 Other Deprecations: replacing builtin and NumPy functions in agg/apply/transform deprecated (FutureWarning)
pilot_tasks: invited by t45 t46 t47 t48 t10 t13
notes: Pilot RPT tasks ask for mean/median/count mostly; ask for std/var explicitly in the full study

name: Iterating groupby with a list of length 1 yields 1-tuples
description: for key, g in df.groupby(["plan"]) gives key as scalar on 2.x; the removals list says 1-tuples for the level-list case and get_group with tuple. Keys used for labels or dict lookups change.
minimal_example_idea: for k, g in df.groupby(["plan"]): out[k] = g.amount.sum()
warn_evidence: 3.0 #other-removals lines on iterating over groupby and get_group; 3.0 other deprecations: groups() keys for list of length 1; exact 2.x warning not verified
notes: Verify by execution which pandas version flips the key to a tuple (plain-column case vs level case)

name: groupby sum/mean float summation without Kahan compensation
description: Last floating-point digits can differ for sorted keys on float columns.
notes: Handle with tolerance in the oracle; classify as numeric noise, not drift

name: SeriesGroupBy.agg no longer pins group name; sum overflow gives inf; median/any with NaT fixes
description: Assorted result changes in groupby from enforced deprecations and bug fixes.
minimal_example_idea: groupby.sum on very large ints; groupby.any on NaT
notes: Low priority

name: concat(sort=False) with DatetimeIndex leaves columns unsorted
description: With all-DatetimeIndex inputs the non-concatenation axis was sorted even if sort=False; now not. Internal concat fixes change apply/shift/join/str.cat row order too.
minimal_example_idea: pd.concat([a, b], axis=1, sort=False) with date indexes
warn_evidence: 3.0 notes: unspecified sort deprecated, warns only when it would change the result; exact 2.x warning not verified
pilot_tasks: t22 t23 t31 t32 (concat/merge of time data)
notes: Order differences are order-only unless the program indexes by position

name: DataFrame.value_counts(sort=False) keeps input order
description: Previously sorted by row labels; now first-appearance order. Also Series.value_counts(sort=False) for str dtype respects the flag.
pilot_tasks: invited by t02 t34 t45

name: nlargest uses a stable sort (ties keep original order)
description: Which tied rows are returned by nlargest/head after sort changes.
minimal_example_idea: df.nlargest(2, "amount") with tied amounts; groupby().apply(lambda g: g.nlargest(...))
pilot_tasks: t25 t26 t27 t28 (top-N with ties)
notes: Need tied values in fixtures; pilot fixtures not checked for ties

name: DataFrame.stack default future_stack=True
description: NA rows are kept, no sorting, no float coercion of columns when stacking several levels.
minimal_example_idea: df.stack() on frame with NaN cells
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.1.0 introduced future_stack; 3.0 removals: specifying False raises FutureWarning; whether 2.3.3 warns on a call without argument: not verified
notes: Verify warning by execution

name: concat dtype rules: empty and all-NA entries no longer ignored
description: Result dtype after concat with empty or all-NA frames changes (e.g. int stays int / object appears).
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.1.0 Other Deprecations: concat with all-NA columns discarded in dtype determination (FutureWarning); pilot regex expects message "concatenation with empty or all-NA entries"
pilot_tasks: invited by t31 t32 t35

name: Bug fixes that change values: qcut boundaries, concat int+bool, pivot_table values/margins, unstack(sort=False), join row order
description: Fixed behaviours change results of correct-looking code: qcut boundary assignment, concat of int and bool no longer casts bools, pivot_table with values also in index/columns, DataFrame.join with list of Series row order.
minimal_example_idea: pd.qcut(df.amount, 4) bin edge values; pd.pivot_table(df, values="amount", index="category", columns="status", margins=True, dropna=False)
notes: Per-bug lists are long (hundreds of lines); only the ones matching task families are listed here

name: Index.join(how=left/right) keeps the result index dtype
description: No cast to object for mixed-dtype index joins; flows to align, join, merge, str.cat.
minimal_example_idea: a.join(b, how="left") with int and str-like index
notes: Mostly dtype-only

name: Automatic downcasting of object results removed (replace, fillna, ffill, bfill, where, mask, clip)
description: Object-dtype results are no longer silently downcast to numeric. Later arithmetic, sort and comparisons on the column can differ.
pilot_tasks: invited by t09 t39 t41 t42 t44
notes: Pilot t39 encodes status via mapping; no drift attributed

name: NaN vs NA in nullable Float64/pyarrow float arithmetic
description: pd.Series([0, np.nan], dtype="Float64") / 0 gives NA, so isna() is True for 0/0 results.
minimal_example_idea: df.convert_dtypes() then a ratio with zero denominators and isna().sum()
notes: Only with nullable dtypes: convert_dtypes, dtype_backend, Float64

name: No dtype inference from pandas objects, Index.insert, setting an Index
description: Constructors given a Series/Index no longer re-infer object to numeric/datetime; Index.insert keeps object.
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.2.0 Other Deprecations (inference in constructors, Index.insert, setting Index into DataFrame)

name: value_counts on object dtype: result index not re-inferred
description: Index of value_counts stays object instead of int/datetime.
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.2.0 Other Deprecations (value_counts object dtype inference)

name: Extension-dtype Series arithmetic along columns keeps NA (Int64, boolean)
description: DataFrame comparison with an extension-dtype Series yields NA instead of True/False where a value is missing.
notes: Needs nullable dtypes

name: Rank and where/mask result dtypes for nullable and extension dtypes
description: rank keeps NA and returns UInt64 on numpy-nullable dtypes; where/mask dtype changes for extension other.
notes: Only with nullable dtypes

name: Categorical: map na_action default None, replace no longer adds categories
description: Categorical.map(na_action) default changed; replace with Categorical dtype no longer introduces categories.
minimal_example_idea: cat.map(lambda v: "x" if pd.isna(v) else v) ; cat_series.replace("a","z")

name: Reductions with axis=None reduce over both axes
description: np.sum(df), df.sum(axis=None) return a scalar, not a per-column Series.
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.1.0 Other Deprecations: axis=None reductions (FutureWarning); pilot regex expects "axis=None is deprecated"
pilot_tasks: invited by t45 t46 t47

name: Integer slice on a float index is positional
description: ser[1:3] on a float-valued index changes from label-based to positional.
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.1.0 Other Deprecations (integer slice on floating index)
notes: Rare in LLM data-wrangling code

name: Series[int] always label-based
description: Integer keys never fall back to position on non-integer indexes: a KeyError (loud) in most cases; silent only when the integer label exists but meant a position.
warn_evidence: whatsnew v2.1.0 Other Deprecations (positional indexing on Series with __getitem__)
notes: Likely mostly loud (hypothesis, confirm by execution); kept for completeness

name: Logical operations with lists, Series with mismatched index
description: &, |, ^ with lists/tuples disallowed; no auto cast to object for mismatched Series indexes.
notes: Mostly loud

name: List arithmetic, Index vs Series comparison, np ufuncs on Index, tuple subclasses
description: Series + list wraps list as Series(list).array; Index == Series returns Series; np.isinf(Index) returns Index; namedtuples hash as tuple.
notes: Low expected effect

name: Row-wise reductions on bool+numeric mixes use NumPy dtypes (3.1)
description: sum/prod/min/max/mean(axis=1) on frames mixing bool and numeric columns can overflow or lose precision.

name: Rolling var/std/skew/kurt/sem numerical fixes
description: Rolling.var, std, skew, kurt, sem change in later digits or formula (sem divisor fixed) versus 2.3.

name: Groupby quantile nearest, median with NaT, corr>1.0, combine_first int precision
description: Assorted bug fixes that change numbers.
notes: Low priority
